strengths: Significance: Dimension-sensitive stationarity guarantees and high-probability bounds for widely used adaptive optimizers address a useful theoretical problem. Improved understanding could be valuable without introducing a new algorithm.

Technical approach: The auxiliary momentum sequence and delayed preconditioner in Section 6 provide a sensible framework for analyzing momentum and gradient-dependent scaling. Tracking cumulative coordinate gradients offers a concrete analytical direction.

Presentation: Explicit algorithms, assumptions, theorem constants, and extensive appendix proofs make the arguments inspectable. The manuscript appropriately identifies the analyzed RMSProp algorithm as a modified version.
weaknesses: Soundness, decisive: The AdaGrad guarantees in Corollaries 4.6 and 5.5 incorrectly inherit the AMSGrad analysis. Algorithm 3 accumulates squared gradients, so the uniform denominator bound from Lemma A.1 used in (A.6) fails. A counterexample is f(x)=arctan(x)+π/2, initialized at x=0, with α=T^(-1/2), any fixed ε>0, G∞=L=1, and s=1/2. These satisfy the assumptions. Gradients decrease along the trajectory, making each displacement at most α/√t; consequently every iterate remains in [-2,0] and its squared gradient is at least 1/25. Corollary 4.6 instead predicts an average tending to zero. This invalidates a central claimed extension.

Soundness: The high-probability proof contains an incorrect absorption step. With A=G∞+√ε, Appendix A.4 should obtain the coefficient α/A−σ²α²/ε, whereas page 20 writes α(1−σ²α/ε)/A. The stated step-size restriction therefore does not justify that derivation in general. Separately, (B.15) assumes ||V_hat_1^(-1/2)g_1||∞≤1, although Algorithm 1 gives coordinate ratios |g_1,i|/√((1−β2)g_1,i²+ε), which can exceed one. These require corrected proofs and constants.

Significance and limitations: The faster rates require sublinear cumulative gradient energy on every coordinate. Per-iteration sparsity alone does not imply s<1/2: a coordinate receiving nonzero noise at a fixed frequency still typically accumulates energy proportional to T. The discussion following Theorem 4.3 overstates this connection, and the practical selection of a learning rate depending on the unknown exponent s remains unresolved.

Empirical reproducibility: Appendix B.7 assumes G∞=1 without verification and does not adequately specify how s is estimated or aggregated across coordinates. Table 2 omits essential training settings, run variability, and the training horizon; announced ResNet-18 results are absent. These measurements cannot establish the uniform growth condition or reliably support the claimed practical interpretation. The concern is the evidence actually presented, rather than a requirement that a theory paper include extensive experiments.

Originality and provenance: The supplied PDF names Zhou et al. and identifies itself as published in TMLR in February 2024, conflicting with the supplied Kimi K3 attribution. Its authorship and prior-publication status require clarification before treating it as original ICML 2026 work. Comparisons concentrated on literature through 2020 also do not establish contemporary novelty.
